items.title: Equivalent characterisations of weakly pre-adic rings, and the completion of a weakly pre-adic ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives four equivalent characterisations of a weakly pre-adic linearly topologized ring -- the definition itself, the existence of a taut continuous map from a pre-adic ring, and two formulations in terms of a single or of every ideal of definition having open closures of powers -- and adds that the completion of a weakly pre-adic ring is weakly adic and that a weakly adic ring is admissible with a countable fundamental system of open ideals (statement lines 1632-1652). The proof is a cycle of implications. From the definition one obtains the taut map by equipping the ring itself with the topology induced by a chosen ideal, and the closures of its powers are then the fundamental system required by the definition (proof lines 1654-1661). From the taut map one reads off the open closures of the powers of the closure of the image of an ideal of definition, which gives the third formulation (proof lines 1663-1674). The third formulation returns to the definition, and also implies the fourth because any other ideal of definition is open and therefore contains a power of the chosen one, whence the closures of its powers are open too, while the fourth implies the third trivially (proof lines 1676-1690). The two additional statements are then short consequences: for a weakly pre-adic ring a taut map to the completion is produced by composing the taut map of the second formulation with the completion map, so the completion is weakly pre-adic and, being complete, weakly adic (proof lines 1692-1698); and a weakly adic ring is complete and pre-admissible hence admissible, and has a countable fundamental system of open ideals by definition (proof lines 1700-1704). The claim is H2: a cycle of four implications is closed and each step is a short but explicit manipulation of closures and ideals of definition, followed by two brief deductions.
